However, unlike these unreliable and partial witnesses, who only tried to make Mitar Vasiljevic's situation even more difficult and who is the only one who is held accountable, regrettably, for their tragedy, there is a testimony which is crucial for this event and I'm referring to the testimony given by VG79. The Prosecutor dedicated only one single sentence to this witness by saying only that he had observed the event from the other side of the river, without making any comment on this statement. It was only in the oral submissions by Mr. Groome, probably because of the Defence final brief in respect of this witness, that we heard Mr. Groome saying that although he did believe this witness, he also believed that he couldn't see the event very well because of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. distance and also because of the fact that he had already given the binoculars to a friend who spent more time observing the event. If we analyse carefully this testimony, we can come up with some very important facts. Despite the fact that the witness was on the other side of the river, some 40 or 400 or 500 metres away, he was observing the event quite closely through his binoculars up to the moment when the shots were heard. This is -- this is a significant and crucial moment for the description of this event. When we bear in mind the fact that witness VG79 recognised two individuals in the group of seven individuals who were lined up on the bank of the Drina, Meho Dzafic and Amir Kurtalic, those were the only two whom he actually knew, and that he was also able that one of the armed individuals was fair and had fair hair, later he concluded that this could have been Milan Lukic. If we, furthermore, bear in mind the fact that he was able to see that one of the weapons was a sniper rifle and that one of them was an automatic rifle, it is quite clear that he was very well positioned to follow and to see what was going on. Furthermore, he knew Mitar Vasiljevic very well, that is not in dispute, and he would have surely recognised Mitar Vasiljevic if he had been one of the three soldiers whom he had seen quite clearly and who were standing behind the line of seven civilians. He also saw them at the moment they opened fire. He mentioned in his statement to the investigator that he had seen seven civilians and three soldiers. This was explained by him before the Court that he was not sure about the fourth soldier, that is the fourth uniformed individual, because he would only see him intermittently as they were moving towards the river. It seemed to him at moments that there were three of them and at moments that there were four of them. However, at the bank the river, he didn't see the fourth soldier. It is his assumption that he remained somewhere in the woods, standing on the left, as looking from the position that he was at. This is a -- the probable explanation of Vasiljevic's testimony, who declared that he was in a state of shock, that he felt embarrassed and that he did not approach the scene. So it is obvious that he remained in the woods and we can be certain that he was not one of the soldiers who were marked by VG79, I'm referring to Exhibit D1 which you had an opportunity to see. Exhibit D1 was provided by the witness to the investigators at the time he gave the statement. Mr. Groome tried to explain this in greater detail by using the diagram made by VG32. According to this diagram none of the soldiers -- out of the soldiers who were there, the second one looking from the left, and who was in the woods, was therefore behind the trees. He said that, according to -- that is to VG32, that Mitar Vasiljevic was third from the left. But it was Witness VG79 who stated that he was not able to see the soldier who was at the far left end, on his side. This could only have been Mitar Vasiljevic, not only because of this explanation but also because of the fact that the witness, this witness, would have surely recognised Mitar Vasiljevic had he been amongst the three soldiers who opened fire. It was only after the shooting started that he handed over the binoculars to his friend. He had seen everything that was relevant and crucial and it is quite important to realise that he was able to see well, and that he claimed that Meho Dzafic whom he was able to recognise in the group of seven civilians, he also saw an unknown civilian who was standing close to Meho Dzafic. When we bear in mind the testimony of the two survivors who noticed that Meho fell down before they heard the shots coming from automatic rifles, we can conclude that Milan Lukic killed one more individual from this group before Meho Dzafic was killed, before his soldiers opened fire and before he opened fire again. Witness VG79 was quite categorical about this. The testimony of this witness excludes the reasonable doubt that Mitar Vasiljevic, apart from physical presence, had any other type of participation in this event, which involved the killing of number of people. If one should try to establish whether it was possible for him to prevent this crime in any way, we, the Defence, submit that it would have been quite impossible, even if he had a weapon, and also, in view -- in light of the behaviour of Milan Lukic's group, and also in light of the statement given by witnesses VG14 and 32, who in response to a question put to them by the Defence during the cross-examination, that is whether they thought that anyone could have had any influence on Milan Lukic on that occasion, to order him anything or to cause him to change his decision, the witnesses responded with, "No" in case of witness VG32. And in response to an even more direct question, they replied that there could not have been an individual of that kind in their vicinity. The other witness replied to the same question by saying,"No, not when it comes to the people who were around him." One also has to note that the Drina River does not bend on this -- in this area, the area of the village of Musici and that that witness had a very clear and unobstructed view of the event.
